name: Valentine's Day
seo_title: Valentine's Day Charcuterie Board Ideas (For Two + Galentine's)
description: Valentine's Day charcuterie board ideas: a heart-shaped board for two, a salami rose, a chocolate dessert board, a Galentine's board for friends, and how much to buy.
answer: A Valentine's board for two needs less than you think: about 4 oz each of cheese and meat per person if it's dinner, 2 oz each if dinner follows. Shape it like a heart, roll salami into a rose, use red and pink (strawberries, raspberries, prosciutto, pomegranate), and finish with dark chocolate and a sparkling rosé.

ideas.title: The Heart Board for Two
ideas.text: A heart of Brie, aged Gouda and a salami rose, with strawberries, raspberries, dark chocolate and honey. One small board and one bottle of sparkling rosé or Pinot Noir.

ideas.title: The Galentine's Board
ideas.text: A bigger, brighter board: whipped feta, burrata, prosciutto, pink grapefruit, strawberries, pistachios and shortbread, with a pitcher of something sparkling.

ideas.title: The Chocolate Dessert Board
ideas.text: Dark chocolate, chocolate-covered strawberries, a triple-crème, salted caramels, shortbread, brandied cherries and a small pour of port.

shapes.name: Heart Board
steps: Lay a heart outline of crackers or folded prosciutto on a round or square board.
Fill it with cheese, a salami rose and berries, keeping the reds and pinks next to the white cheeses.
Set a small bowl of chocolate or honey in the center.

plan.what: Order any specialty cheese and buy chocolate, crackers, jam and the wine.
Buy cheese, meat and berries. Chill the wine.
Wash and dry the berries and make the salami rose. Cover and chill.
Take the Gouda out of the fridge, then the Brie 30 minutes later, and build the board.

faq.q: How much charcuterie do I need for two people?
faq.a: If the board is dinner, about 4 oz each of cheese and meat per person, so 8 oz of each in total. If you're going out to dinner after, 2 oz of each per person is plenty. Two cheeses and two meats are enough.

faq.q: How do you make a salami rose?
faq.a: Fold thin salami slices over the rim of a small wine glass, overlapping each one by about half, in three or four layers. Turn the glass over onto the board and lift it off, then tuck a basil or mint leaf at the base.

faq.q: What wine goes with a Valentine's charcuterie board?
faq.a: Sparkling rosé or Champagne works with almost everything on it. For a still wine, choose a light red like Pinot Noir. If the board ends with dark chocolate, a small glass of port is the classic match.

faq.q: How do you make a heart-shaped charcuterie board?
faq.a: Outline a heart on the board with crackers or folded prosciutto, then fill it in with cheese, a salami rose and red fruit. A heart-shaped cookie cutter also turns cheese slices into hearts in seconds.

faq.q: What goes on a Galentine's Day board?
faq.a: Pretty, shareable things: whipped feta or burrata, prosciutto, pink grapefruit and strawberries, pistachios, shortbread or pink cookies, and a sparkling drink. Plan about 2 oz each of cheese and meat per guest if there's other food, 3 oz if the board is the party.
